drhp.business: Adisoft designs, develops, procures, assembles, tests, installs and commissions automated assembly lines, material handling machines, robotic work cells and special purpose machinery, integrating shop-floor equipment with the IT layer (PLC/SCADA/GOT/IoT/MES) to automate industrial processes. business_ops.supply_chain_integration: Backward integration through in-house design & development (complete design lifecycle - mechanical/electrical system design, control architecture and simulation) using tools such as E-PLAN, SolidWorks, AutoCAD and ZW Cad, and in-house assembly, testing and quality assurance at the MIDC Bhosari, Pune assembly unit (co-located inventory to minimize material movement). Automation-solutions revenue is project-based and integrated end-to-end, while a trading stream procures automation products (PLC, HMI, Servo, AC Drive, digital picking system components) from various suppliers and delivers them in original form. Major raw materials are sourced indigenously, predominantly from Maharashtra (79.45%, 70.98%, 78.82% and 83.83% of total raw material purchases for period ended Oct 31, 2025 and FY2025, FY2024, FY2023). No long-term supply contracts with suppliers. Forward-side lifecycle support includes 12-month warranty, repair/replacement, system upgrades, retrofitting, AMC and on-site installation, commissioning and troubleshooting.

concerns_observed: Weak earnings-to-cash conversion: operating cash flow was negative in two of three fiscals - Rs (641.32) lakh (FY24) and Rs (72.47) lakh (FY25) - despite rising PAT; FY25 trade receivables of Rs 5,613.24 lakh equalled 42.62% of revenue.
Heavy automotive-sector dependence: the automotive segment was 59.95% / 78.61% / 72.48% / 64.32% of revenue (Oct'25 stub / FY25 / FY24 / FY23), tying demand to auto-industry capex cycles.
Customer concentration with no long-term contracts: top customer 43.39-50.86%, top 5 customers 62.21-67.40% and top 10 customers 70.18-77.19% of revenue across the reported periods.
Supplier concentration: top 10 suppliers were 76.57-85.54% of raw-material purchases and Maharashtra sourcing 70.98-83.83%, with no long-term supply contracts.
Geographic concentration - Haryana 51.05-64.20% and Maharashtra ~30% of revenue - and a single Pune assembly unit; the registered office, assembly unit and two sales/service offices are all rented.
Rising share of lower-margin trading of automation products (23.68% of revenue in FY23 to 38.69% in the Oct'25 stub) may dilute blended margins versus the customised-solutions business.

Related-party density: recurring Rs 7 lakh annual commissions to the promoters' relatives (mother and sister), Rs 70 lakh professional fees to each promoter in FY24, a Rs 173.43 lakh 'reimbursement of statutory dues' to the CFO's spouse (Sagar Dilip Dale) in the stub, rent to the promoter's father, purchases from the AIOI associate (Rs 178.27-465.08 lakh) and promoter unsecured loans (Rs 206.50 lakh outstanding).

Ten-year history of Companies Act non-compliance (Sections 77, 129, 137 - non-preparation of cash-flow and consolidated financial statements for FY2020-21 to 2023-24, non-filing of Form CHG-1) with compounding applications only submitted, and restated consolidated financials provided by a peer-reviewed CA who is NOT the statutory auditor.
Governance depth: directors have no prior listed-company experience and the five-member board has only two independent directors.

A 1200:1 bonus issue on September 05, 2025 (within the 18-month regulatory window) at nil consideration; promoters' average acquisition cost of Rs 0.01 per share sits far below an as-yet-undisclosed issue price.

Objects of the Issue not appraised by any bank/FI, most vendor works (RMC/steel, furniture, laptops) not yet placed as firm orders, and no alternate funding identified; ISO 9001:2015 not yet certified and the trademark is unregistered.

Group company Kenmei Automation Private Limited (director-interested, similar business) was struck off on December 03, 2025; the DRHP also notes past delays in payment of dues to financial institutions and past challenges adhering to GST, EPF and ESI provisions.

strengths_observed: Consistent high growth: revenue rose from Rs 7,554.27 lakh (FY2022-23) to Rs 10,326.85 lakh (FY2023-24) to Rs 13,171.78 lakh (FY2024-25), roughly 32% two-year CAGR, with PAT climbing Rs 607.93 -> 1,175.57 -> 1,611.08 lakh.
Margin expansion alongside scale: EBITDA margin improved from 11.01% (FY23) to 15.56% (FY24) to 16.45% (FY25) and PAT margin from 8.05% to 11.38% to 12.23%.
Strong return ratios across the reported fiscals: ROE 33.10% / 43.12% / 39.11%, ROCE 27.25% / 32.35% / 29.11% and RONW 28.43% / 35.47% / 32.71% for FY23/FY24/FY25.
Net-cash-leaning balance sheet at the stub date: cash Rs 2,382.52 lakh against total debt Rs 1,968.21 lakh and net worth Rs 5,303.16 lakh as at Oct 31, 2025, with nil promoter pledge.
Fresh-issue-only offer (no OFS): proceeds accrue to the Company - debt repayment Rs 1,000 lakh, new Pune factory Rs 3,777.34 lakh and working capital Rs 1,000 lakh - rather than a promoter cash-out.
Clean disclosed litigation record (nil count/amount against Company, promoters, directors, KMP and group company) and low contingent liabilities of Rs 260.14 lakh, equal to 4.91% of net worth.

In-house design-to-assembly integration (E-PLAN, SolidWorks, AutoCAD; MIDC Bhosari, Pune assembly unit) plus a February 2021 tripartite JV linkage with AIOI Systems Co. Ltd., Japan (24% associate stake).

Working-capital recovery visible in the stub: operating cash flow of Rs 1,233.54 lakh for the seven months ended Oct 31, 2025 after two negative-CFO fiscals, and an order book of Rs 4,432.61 lakh as on April 15, 2026.
